items.heading: ### RDBMS naming prefixes
items.text: A non-derived `DataMember` with `identifier=true` gets one non-unique btree index (`IDX_<hash>`) on its column. The generator creates no index for foreign-key columns, and the model has no syntax to declare other indexes; add them with a hand-written schema changeset (see [schema evolution](schema-evolution.md)).
items.evidence: target/judo-ng-read/wt/runtime__judo-tatami-base/judo-tatami-asm2rdbms/src/main/java/hu/blackbelt/judo/tatami/asm2rdbms/zeta/rules/AttributeRules.java:273-296 (eAttributeToIndex creates RdbmsIndex, sqlName IDX_<md5>, no unique flag); ReferenceRules.java has no index creation

items.heading: ### Common Generator Parameters
items.text: With `useCache=true` a failed UI validation can show only `{}: {}` and 'Verify UI model is presented', hiding the cause. To see the real error, build with `-DuseCache=false -DvalidateModels=true`.

items.heading: ### Step 3: Manual Migration Scripts (Optional)
items.text: Entity tables are named `T_<NAMESPACE>_<ENTITY>` and columns `C_<ATTRIBUTE>` (check the generated changelog for the exact names). To insert a hand-written changeset, run the plugin goals `judo-rdbms-schema:generate` and then `judo-rdbms-schema:execute`; `judo.sh schema-upgrade` does both in one step and cannot take a changeset in between.

items.heading: ### Docker Compose
items.text: PostgreSQL's default `max_connections` (100) can run out after a few application restarts (`sorry, too many clients`). Raise it in the compose file, for example `command: ["postgres", "-c", "max_connections=300"]`.
items.evidence: app: ~/Projects/webshop-test/deploy/docker-compose.yml:12 (max_connections=300, comment: the application keeps several connection pools)

items.heading: ### RDBMS naming prefixes
items.text: Foreign-key columns get no index from the generator. A derived member or query that joins or filters over them scans the referenced table, which becomes slow with many rows; add the indexes by hand in a schema changeset.

items.heading: ### `judo.sh build` flag reference
items.text: | `-f` | `--build-frontend-module` | Build the frontend React module only. The Karaf package is not rebuilt, so a running application keeps serving the old frontend: after a frontend change that a running application must show, run `./judo.sh build -i` (full build, with Karaf) and restart with `./judo.sh start`.

items.heading: ### 6. Email (SMTP)
items.text: **Local testing with Mailpit:** run a mail catcher such as Mailpit locally; the app only knows an SMTP host and port, so for local runs point them at `localhost:1025` (no TLS) in `judo-karaf.env`. Also set `JUDO_PLATFORM_MAIL_SMTP_USER` and `JUDO_PLATFORM_MAIL_SMTP_PASSWORD` to any value, with `JUDO_PLATFORM_MAIL_SMTP_AUTH=false`: the mail service (`JavaMailSenderActivator`) is only created when the log SMTP server is on or user, password and host are all set, so host and port alone give no `EmailService`.
items.replaces: **Local testing with Mailpit:** run a mail catcher such as Mailpit locally; the app only knows an SMTP host and port, so for local runs point them at `localhost:1025` (no authentication, no TLS) in `judo-karaf.env`.

items.heading: ### When No Manual Step Is Needed
items.text: Adding a **stored** member (for example a new attribute) to an entity needs **no** manual migration or `schema-upgrade` run for a fresh database (empty or newly created, so Liquibase creates everything). For an existing database with rows, the new column is filled with NULL, not with the attribute's model default; for a value other than NULL, write a backfill changeset (see [migration backfill](../../best-practices/backend/migration-backfill-default-where-null.md)).
items.replaces: Adding a **stored** member (for example a new attribute) to an entity needs **no** manual migration or `schema-upgrade` run for a fresh database (empty or newly created, so Liquibase creates everything).
